reason: Not functional: a video thumbnail inside a disclosure summary. The thumbnail shows a still from the video rather than standing for a function, so it is a content image in a control. Its empty alt is the right call, because the summary text carries the label.
Functional: opens the overflow navigation. The link's own text reads "More menu" and the three-dot icon carries no alternative text of its own.
Functional: the store logo links to the site root. The SVG title is the bare brand name, which does not tell a person the link goes home.
Functional: the BBC logo links to the site root, and the announced name "Homepage" is right. But it comes from text beside the logo, and the graphic itself carries no description.

A cover photograph inside a link to the regulations, with "View Title II Regulations" already beside it. The alt describes the picture, quote marks and all, instead of the destination, and the adjacent text makes it redundant anyway.
Functional: a button that opens an advertiser's landing page. The label is the bare product name and says nothing about what pressing it does or where it goes.
Functional: a link to the application portal. The link's own text reads "The Kennel" and the icon beside it has no alternative text.
Functional: the documentation logo links to python.org. The alt is the brand name plus the word "logo", naming the picture rather than the destination.
Functional: an icon-only button that opens the search field. The label names the action, and the SVG title and the button's aria-label agree, so there is one unambiguous reference.
Functional: an icon that is the sole link to an external pagelist tool. The alt names the tool and, in the parenthesis, what it does. Nothing about the drawing.

Functional: the header logo links to the site root, and the alt does start with the destination. But it then describes the flag artwork and transcribes the tagline, which is the visual detail the criteria call irrelevant, at four times the length needed.
Functional: the close control of a multi-select dropdown. The label names both the action and where focus lands, which is the state information a person driving by keyboard actually needs.
Functional: a link to the notifications page. The link's own text reads "Notifications" and the bell icon carries no alternative text.
Functional: the logo links to the site root. The announced name comes from text beside it and the SVG has neither a title nor a label of its own.
Functional: opens the filter panel. The button already displays the text "Filter Options" and the aria-label only repeats it, so nothing was written for the icon itself.

Functional: the logo links to the locale home page, so it is a linked logo. Two correct decisions: the image carries an empty alt and the link is labelled "IKEA Home", which is brand plus destination and the pattern the root README calls high quality.

Functional: the theme toggle in the documentation header. The label names the action and both states it moves between. It carries hidden until the script enables it, which is a progressive enhancement gate rather than an exclusion from assistive technology.
Functional: the logo links to bbc.com. The announced "BBC Homepage" is good text, but it comes from a span beside the logo and the SVG itself has no description.
Functional: the close control of the mobile navigation. The alt names the action rather than the X drawing, and nothing adjacent repeats it.

Functional: a product link in the component browser. The icon is a generic component glyph with an empty alt, correct because the link's own text reads "Core". The redundancy filter applied the right way round.
Functional: the header logo links to the site root. The alt begins "logo of", describing the image rather than saying the link goes home.

Functional, but a share action rather than navigation: the href is a fragment and script posts the page to Facebook. The alt names the service, so a person hears "Facebook" and reasonably expects to be taken there instead of sharing.
Functional: the store logo links to the site root. The SVG title is the bare brand name, with nothing about the destination.

Functional: the logo links to the site home. But the link is labelled "Home" while the SVG inside labels itself "Node.js logo", so there are two competing shipped descriptions and no single reference to score against.
Functional: the submit button of the search form, so the sub-type is a form control rather than a toggle. The alt names the action instead of the magnifier.

Functional: the tracker logo links to the site root. The alt is "homepage", which names where the link goes and says nothing about the snake. Terse, and exactly the criterion the README sets for a linked logo.
Functional: a section accordion. The button already displays "More In This section" and the plus and minus icon has no alternative text of its own.
Functional: a link from Sounds to News. The product icon is correctly aria-hidden and the link's own text carries the label, so there is no alt text to judge.
Functional: the logo links to the site root, with an empty alt because the link's own text reads "Library of Congress". The correct half of the pattern that fi-9511 gets wrong on the same site.
Functional: the previous control of a carousel. The label names the action and the direction, which is all a person needs from an arrow glyph. It is disabled at the first slide, and still announced.
